title: Assessing attention/concentration: reciting months backward
vignette: A 67-year-old woman comes to the office due to difficulty concentrating. She reports repeatedly reading the same page of material due to an inability to focus. She also describes memory problems, stating that it "takes a while to remember another person's name." The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. These are well controlled through diet, exercise, and oral medications. She lives alone and describes her mood as "good." Blood pressure is 127/67 mm Hg and pulse is 65/min. The physician decides to administer a brief cognitive test to assess her difficulty in concentrating. Which of the following elements of cognitive testing would best assess for impaired attention and concentration in this patient?

clues.note: The chief complaint targets ATTENTION/CONCENTRATION specifically - the exam element must test sustained mental focus, not memory or language.
To probe attention/concentration, use a continuous mental-tracking task (reciting months backward, serial 7s, or spelling 'world' backward).

whatMatters: Attention and concentration are best tested with a sustained mental-tracking task: RECITING THE MONTHS OF THE YEAR BACKWARD (or serial 7s, or spelling 'world' backward). Answer C. The other options assess different domains - memory registration/recall, comprehension, remote memory, or language.
strategy: Map each option to a cognitive DOMAIN and pick the one that isolates attention/concentration (continuous manipulation of information). Months-backward = attention. Reject: 3-word recall at 5 min (short-term memory), 3-step command (comprehension), remembering past events (remote/long-term memory), writing a sentence (language).

options.text: Reciting months of the year backwards

eliminations.label: Following a 3-step command - comprehension
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a brief multistep command tests COMPREHENSION (receptive language/executive following). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is over quickly and doesn't require sustained attention/concentration. ✅ Correct if: assessing comprehension/command following.

eliminations.label: Recalling 3 words after 5 minutes - short-term memory (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: registration and delayed recall of 3 words tests SHORT-TERM MEMORY. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it assesses memory encoding/recall, not attention/concentration (which requires continuous mental tracking). ✅ Correct if: testing short-term/working memory recall.

eliminations.label: Remembering past events - remote (long-term) memory
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: recalling life events tests REMOTE/long-term memory. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it does not measure the ability to sustain and manipulate attention. ✅ Correct if: assessing long-term/remote memory.

eliminations.label: Writing a complete sentence - language
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: writing a grammatical sentence tests the LANGUAGE domain. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it evaluates language output, not attention/concentration. ✅ Correct if: assessing language/writing.

reasoning: Attention/concentration require a continuous mental-tracking task
Reciting months backward (like serial 7s or 'world' backward) isolates that ability
-> reciting months of the year backwards; answer C
mechanism: On the mental status exam, different tasks probe different cognitive DOMAINS. ATTENTION and CONCENTRATION are the ability to focus on and continuously manipulate information; they are best tested with sustained mental-tracking tasks such as reciting the MONTHS OF THE YEAR BACKWARD, counting down from 100 by 7s (serial 7s), or spelling a word (e.g., 'world') backward. Reciting months backward is especially useful when a patient has low educational attainment or is uneasy with arithmetic or spelling. In contrast, registering and recalling 3 unrelated words after several minutes tests SHORT-TERM (recent) memory; following a multistep command tests COMPREHENSION; recalling significant life events tests REMOTE (long-term) memory; and writing a sentence tests LANGUAGE. Standardized tools like the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) include a specific attention/concentration section using these tracking tasks. Because this patient's complaint centers on concentration, the months-backward task best targets the domain in question.

difficulty.text: First Aid Psych > mental status exam domains: attention/concentration (serial 7s, months backward, 'world' backward); memory (3-word recall); language; orientation; executive function.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: The complaint is attention/concentration, so choose the continuous mental-tracking task (months backward).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on attention vs memory vs comprehension vs language domains, serial 7s, or MoCA? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: 3-word recall = short-term memory; 3-step command = comprehension; past events = remote memory; sentence = language.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: attention/concentration tests = serial 7s, months of year backward, spell 'world' backward.

memoryHook: To test focus, make the brain juggle in reverse - months (or numbers) backward; recalling 3 words later is memory, not attention.
